deviations.derivation: The packet's booked D4 happy path (two valid 5-face triangular prisms; the recombination a valid single shell) does NOT unblock. With a faithful D1/D2 the recorded FIRST blocker is genuinely removed — instrumentation confirms the open-arc certified-endpoint guard (split.rs open_arc_certified) no longer fires and the four box vertices are collected — but the diagonal halves now refuse UnsupportedEnvelope(ContactReductionDeferred) at split.rs assemble_pending_loops (the unclosed-pending-chain guard, backtrace: assemble_pending_loops:1641 <- dispatch:909 <- run:900). The wall face (B,1) accumulates a duplicate of each box-edge open arc: each of the two box-edge lines (x=2,y=0 and x=0,y=2) is witnessed by TWO FF records (wall x box-face x=2 and wall x box-face y=0 / wall x box-face x=0 and wall x box-face y=2), and the greedy chain builder consumes a duplicate, leaving a chain whose last edge's back is not the first edge's front. The four certified arcs would close the box's wall cross-section quadrilateral ((2,0,0)-(0,2,0)-(0,2,2)-(2,0,2)), but the extra duplicate cannot close. The instrumented unclosed chain: [(2,0,0)->(0,2,0), (0,2,0)->(0,2,2), (0,2,2)->(2,0,2), (2,0,2)->(2,0,0), (2,0,0)->(2,0,2)] on face (B,1).

deviations.derivation: A faithful D1/D2 cannot satisfy the packet's 'resew must pass UNCHANGED' requirement. Collecting the cross-solid EndpointTouch seam corners into certified_points (the mandated D2 collect) also certifies the face-adjacent family's corner-touch FF lines: e.g. box A's x=0 face x box B's y=0 face bound to a SINGLE point (the seam corner (0,0,1)). insert_open_arc_shared then finds one certified point on the carrier, p_min == p_max, and Edge::try_new(&v0, &v0, sub) refuses (backtrace: insert_open_arc_shared Edge::try_new map_err refused <- ff_curve:1117 <- dispatch:921). At base these lines were skipped by the certified-empty seam_skip path (seam_skip = event_cross_solid = true). This is a decision-vs-tree contradiction (SPEC_GAP class): the packet pre-decided both 'cross-solid EndpointTouch points are certified clipping points' and 'resew stays unchanged', and the tree shows they cannot both hold. Fixing it (e.g. skipping single-certified-point arcs, or filtering which EndpointTouch loci certify) is a design decision the packet did not make; I did not extend the design.

notes: RW-VERTEX-CLIP stopped. The D1 filter and D2 collection/dispatch were implemented faithfully and PROVEN to work by temporary instrumentation (removed before revert): the four cross-solid EndpointTouch box vertices flow through the sweep and reach certified_points, and the open-arc certified-endpoint guard no longer fires. But the booked unblock is false in this tree: the diagonal still refuses ContactReductionDeferred, now at assemble_pending_loops (duplicate box-edge open arcs on the wall face cannot close a chain), and — more fundamentally — the mandated cross-solid EndpointTouch collection breaks the packet's required-unchanged resew suite (4/7: certified seam-corner points collapse corner-touch FF lines to a single point and Edge::try_new refuses). Both are stop conditions the packet itself prescribes ('the guard fixture refuses for a DIFFERENT reason than the recorded one'; 'if the fixture's refusal class dissolves'). The dispatch re-route needed a cross-solid guard (event_cross_solid) to keep the landed lib test split_deferred_locus_family_refuses green — its endpoint fixture feeds split_fragments a same-solid Face/Edge pair directly, which must still refuse. I did not extend the design (no D5 arms, no new Refusal/EnvelopeCase), did not touch the Arc1 Coincident arms or the RW-RESEW zero-measure filters, and reverted everything so the tree is green: cargo check -p truck-shapeops clean; cut_boundaries 7/7, boolean_m2 4/4, interior_loop 8/8, resew 7/7 (all at base); lib 46/47 (the recorded environmental healing::tests::step_import); kernel-gates.sh HEAD reports GATE-4 unscaled_legacy 111/111 and all P-3 gates pass. The follow-up packet needs a decision the packet did not make: how a certified clipping point pool interacts with the duplicate/witnessed open arcs (dedupe, or a certified-extreme >= 2-point filter at insert_open_arc_shared), and whether resew's corner-touch FF lines must be excluded from certification.
